question: When two role-swapped queries read the same scene, can the displacement of the same reference box estimate the subject box's localization error?
scope: Only the 111 existing source-own, natural, inventory-proxy records. Each model sees its own platform. Source annotations are opened only after replay and label-free predictions are sealed. The 111 original captions were previously used in development. No target domain, no FINAL, no training.
physical_effect: Choose the highest-prior four-box tuple among tuples where both role queries contain the correct subject and correct reference, using unique annotated-object overlap above 0.25 for eligibility only. Compare the reverse subject's original center and center plus the displacement from the reverse to the forward reference. Keep the reverse subject box's size and yaw. Compare its negative displacement at identical magnitude. Compute squared center error to the official subject and squared discrepancy between queries, finite differences by the exact quadratic identity, oriented IoU and Acc50 saves/losses. Include zero displacements and report missing tuples. This is a favorable diagnostic, never a deployed selection.
label_free_rule: Use the original four subject slots and native forward and reversed pair probabilities from the locked study. For an ordered tuple score unshifted reference overlap times the forward subject overlap with the reverse subject translated by the reference displacement. Subtract the analogous quantity with roles swapped. Use the existing positive/negative mass allocation for raw and alternative shapes. Reference overlap is always evaluated before translation. Average proposed translated centers with the previous horizontal shape tensor and height rule. Also score no translation, opposite sign, and a cyclic permutation of reverse anchors only for the translation vector (keep the pre-shift evidence). Report raw subject selection separately.
decision: Expansion requires source evidence that the measured reference shift improves absolute subject localization on eligible subjects and protects Acc50, with actual transfer to the label-free readout. An improvement in cross-query consistency alone is insufficient. Report using the source proxy limitation.
preserved: original checkpoints, parameter state and full frozen v1, original active sampling, original GT, all failure and fallback rows
